newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks slip on racketeer report.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks slip on racketeer report.

text.p: Tokyo stocks slipped into negative territory on Monday afternoon, hurt by a news agency report that a corporate racketeer told prosecutors that Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd conducted illegal stock deals for him, brokers said.
As of 0423 GMT, the Nikkei average was down 12.50 points or 0.06 percent to 20,511.25. Its September futures shed 20 points to 20,550.
"The market was lacking direction to begin with and the report is worrying investors," said a general manager at a second-tier brokerage.
"We cannot comment right now as we don't know about the Jiji news agency report yet," a Nikko spokesman said, adding that he would check whether the report was true or not.
The president of Nikko Securities, Kichiro Takao, told the firm's annual shareholders' meeting on Friday that he was not aware of any illegal payments by the firm to shareholders.

Nikko shares fell 54 yen to 700 with trade totalling 2.9 million shares, the fifth most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse. A Daiwa spokesman told Reuters that the brokerage had not had time to study the report so could not comment on it.
Daiwa shares were down 39 yen at 910, with trade totalling 2.87 million shares, the sixth most actively traded stock.
An official at Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) made no comment on the Jiji report.
